cases.suggestion: Note: 'HTTP 200' for a successful cancel is not stated in spec.yaml (GAP-02 gives codes only for refusals); accept it as the standard success code or write 'success (2xx)'.
Optional: name the admin request that moves the order to Accepted in the preconditions and the read endpoint (GET /api/order/number/{number}) in step 2, as TC-SCRUM-9-01 and TC-SCRUM-9-12 do.
Optional: name the admin requests in the preconditions and the read endpoint in step 2.
Optional: name the admin request in the preconditions and the read endpoint in step 2.
Optional: name the read endpoint in step 2.
The description still says 'Compare with TC-SCRUM-9-07 (unknown order)'; TC-SCRUM-9-07 is now deprecated and this case does the comparison itself in step 2, so that sentence can go.
Optional: step 2 'Read the order.' - name the read endpoint.
Note: 'HTTP 200' is not stated in spec.yaml; the spec-based result is that the status change succeeds and the new status is shown.
Optional: on a shared environment page 0 with size=50 may not contain A's order if more than 50 cancelled orders exist; say how to find it (sort or page through).

Optional: plan section 4 says 'one partition per status value of the filter'; this case uses NEW (Received) as the representative of the non-cancelled values. That is enough for REQ-SCRUM-9-21 (only the Cancelled filter is required), but ACCEPTED, DELIVERED and REJECTED could be added as further steps if the plan wording is read literally.
Optional: steps 2 and 5 expect 'The order is not cancelled.' - make it observable, for example 'The order still shows Received' (steps 3 and 6 already check it after reload).
Optional: add the tag REQ-SCRUM-9-01 (it is in the description but not in the tags).
Optional: preconditions do not say whether customer A is signed in when opening the tracking page; state it.
Optional: say in the preconditions to note the numbers of orders 1-5 so they can be found in the list on a shared environment.
Optional: with TC-SCRUM-9-38 the 'counts' partition now exists. To make this case self-proving, a read of the figure after step 2 (expected R1 + T) would show the figure updates before the cancel.
Optional: step 3 combines 'open the details' and 'decline'; split it, and say where the status is read (for example 'The admin order details show Declined').

Note: 'Accept and Reject actions are offered' is inferred from REQ-SCRUM-9-23, not stated for Received orders in spec.yaml; the spec-based results are step 2 (status can be changed) and 'no action to set Cancelled'.

Optional: step 4 'Go to checkout, choose takeaway and place the order' could be split into 'open checkout' and 'choose takeaway and submit' so the checkout page has its own expected result. Device list in the description matches plan section 6 exactly (6 devices).
Optional: Received is the representative of the 'counts' partition (Received, Accepted, Delivered per CHG-17); one representative is enough for equivalence partitioning.
